_comment: Hardened synthetic persona for memory benchmarking. All facts fictional. Designed to stress what a small verbatim persona cannot: temporal contradictions (current vs. stale), multi-hop relations, and distractor noise. Every gold answer is stated in a session message. Each eval question carries a gold 'answer' for the LLM judge plus 'keywords' for the legacy keyword scorer.
name: Priya Sharma
description: Robotics engineer, recently relocated. Designed to test current-vs-stale fact resolution, multi-hop relations, and retrieval under distractor noise.

facts.text: Priya currently lives in Denver (moved from Portland last spring)
Priya currently works at Cobalt Robotics as a robotics engineer (left Northwind Logistics in March)
Priya leads the perception team at Cobalt Robotics
Priya's sister is Anita; Anita is an architect
Anita's husband (Priya's brother-in-law) is Raj, a cardiologist
Anita and Raj live in Chicago
Priya's parents are Deepak and Sunita, who live in Portland
Priya's best friend is Lena, who works at Stripe
Priya owns a Cannondale Synapse road bike
Priya's cat is named Biryani, a tabby
Priya's favorite food is palak paneer
Priya is reading The Overstory by Richard Powers
Priya is learning Japanese for a trip to Kyoto in November

messages.content: Hey, I'm Priya Sharma. Still settling into Denver after the move from Portland last spring — boxes everywhere.
Welcome to Denver! How's the move treating you?
Chaotic but good. Work changed too — I left Northwind Logistics back in March and started as a robotics engineer at Cobalt Robotics.
Big year of changes. Are you enjoying the new role?
Yeah. The Denver hiking helps with the stress — did the Mount Falcon trail last weekend, gorgeous views.
My sister Anita is flying in next week with her husband Raj. He's a cardiologist, always on call.
That'll be a nice visit. Where are they coming from?
Anita and Raj live in Chicago, so we don't see each other much.
Is the rest of the family nearby?
No — my parents, Deepak and Sunita, still live back in Portland. They refused to leave their garden.
Caught up with my best friend Lena last night. She just got promoted at Stripe, so proud of her.
Congrats to Lena! Do you two share hobbies?
She keeps pushing me to try climbing, but I'm loyal to my road bike — a Cannondale Synapse.
Sounds like a good week.
Eh, weather's been gray and I'm behind on everything, but I'll survive.
Reading The Overstory by Richard Powers right now — slow but gorgeous.
Great pick. What else are you up to?
Made palak paneer for dinner — my favorite, total childhood comfort food.
Any new hobbies since the move?
Picked the violin back up after years. Playing scales badly every night, but it's something.
Big news: I finally adopted a cat! Her name's Biryani — a little tabby with strong opinions.
Amazing! How's work going?
Cobalt's got me leading the perception team now. Wild how fast that happened since I joined.
That's a fast ramp-up.
Honestly I still miss Portland's food scene, but Denver's growing on me.
Trying to learn Japanese before a trip to Kyoto in November. The verb conjugations are kicking me.
Exciting trip! Any travel for work too?
They sent me to a robotics conference in Boston last month — met a few Cobalt clients there.
Raj — my brother-in-law, the cardiologist — gave me unsolicited heart-health advice all weekend, ha.
Family, right? How was the rest of the visit?
Lovely. Anita's an architect, so she spent the whole time critiquing Denver's buildings. She designed a library in Chicago last year.
It'll be one year in Denver next month. Cobalt Robotics, Biryani the cat, the Cannondale — life actually feels settled now.
